CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper lobe lung nodule

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a former smoker presenting with an incidentally discovered right upper lobe lung nodule. Patient reports experiencing an intermittent cough for approximately three months, initially occurring while loading hay for horses. Subsequently developed a cold prompting visit to primary care physician. PCP diagnosed bronchitis and ordered chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia, which revealed a lung nodule. CT scan was obtained for confirmation, and patient was referred to pulmonology. Cough has since resolved. Patient denies current dyspnea, chest pain, or fever.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, dyspnea, fever, or other acute symptoms. Cough has resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly

ALLERGIES
Allergies not reported in visit

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. Denies family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. Denies family history of pneumonia or lung infections.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Former smoker, quit approximately 7 years ago. Currently exercises regularly with frequent biking. Works with horses. Denies current tobacco use. Active lifestyle maintained.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 124/76 mmHg, heart rate 70 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, afebrile
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats
Extremities: Skin pink, warm, and dry; no edema to lower extremities; mild swelling of knuckles on third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis; pulses intact in all extremities; brisk capillary refill

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule: Order pulmonary function tests for baseline assessment. Schedule PET-CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Recommend video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for nodule resection with wedge of lung tissue. Procedure under general anesthesia, approximately 1.5 hours, three small incisions on right chest. Post-operative chest tube until post-op day 1 with removal at bedside. Hospital admission for one night. Patient counseled on risks, benefits, and alternatives and agrees to proceed.

Rheumatoid arthritis: Continue follow-up with rheumatology. Continue methotrexate therapy as prescribed.
